record.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
record.summary: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), then released a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization. The linked Lean scope describes a subexponential exact-counting bound for fixed-k canonical k-CNF formulas, a formalized statement that would contradict ETH if its definitions and scope match the standard conjecture. OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result; the group’s participation is not certification. Independent mathematical review, a reproduced build and practical algorithmic consequences remain unestablished.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On October 26, OpenAI published an announcement describing an AI-generated ETH refutation and linked a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization in its public repository.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that its system produced a refutation of ETH. The linked Lean scope states that, for each fixed k at least 2, a deterministic machine exactly counts satisfying assignments of canonical k-CNF formulas in subexponential time with polynomial space; the manuscript states a sharper exponent for m clauses. The currently inspected theorem source contains a proof body, while a separate comparator challenge file retains a sorry placeholder. This repository inspection does not establish a pinned, reproducible build, full dependency closure, or correspondence to standard ETH.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result and that the group requested public raw materials; their participation does not certify the claim.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Community reports now describe pinned independent executions and a port checked by multiple kernels, but no independent conclusion establishes that the formalized machine predicate is equivalent to textbook ETH or that the informal paper follows from the checked statement; no practical speedup is established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In comments on the reviewer-maintained ETH discussion site, independent contributors report pinned native Lean executions of the labs’ formalizations and a port of OpenAI’s proof to complexitylib’s standard multitape machine accepted by Lean’s judge and three additional checkers, including rejection of a planted wrong statement. The reports explicitly leave the correspondence between the formalized machine predicates and textbook ETH as an interpretive step; the research desk did not rerun these artifacts.

evidence_gaps.description: The community now reports pinned independent executions and a formal port to a standard multitape-machine library with multiple checkers, but the research desk did not rerun these artifacts. The correspondence from the checked formal statements to the informal manuscript and textbook ETH remains unestablished as a theorem.
The reported subexponential counting bound does not establish a practical speedup on real instances or polynomial-time solvability.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded theorem genuinely refutes ETH for standard exact k-SAT, many conditional lower-bound arguments across theoretical computer science would require reassessment. The score reflects consequence if true; independent proof review and practical algorithmic impact are not established.
limitations: The theorem remains an OpenAI-reported claim; independent correctness and standard-ETH correspondence are not established.

The current main-branch theorem source has a visible proof body, but the repository was not pinned and no Lean build or full import-closure review was performed; a separate comparator challenge file retains a sorry placeholder.
Subexponential time is not polynomial time; the announcement does not establish P = NP or practical speedups.
The external group’s involvement is explicitly not certification; the result awaits independent examination.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports a Lean-formalized, subexponential exact-counting result for fixed-k canonical k-CNF, which would contradict ETH if its statement and scope match the standard conjecture.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Oct 26 release and linked scope are directly observable. In the current mutable main branch, the inspected theorem source contains a proof body; a separate comparator challenge interface retains a sorry placeholder. Neither a pinned project build nor theorem correctness was established.
technical.mechanism: The theorem source Final.lean contains a compiled_exact_count_and_sat proof body for the described deterministic exact-counting result, followed by a wrapper theorem. The separate ComparatorChallenges/SubexponentialSAT.lean interface is a comparator challenge and still contains sorry; this is not the theorem source. The repository was not pinned, the full import closure was not audited and no Lean build was run.
technical.regime: Fixed k≥2 canonical k-CNF; the scope page states an exponent O_k(n(log log n)^2/sqrt(log n)) plus polynomial encoding-length factors, and polynomial space.
technical.reproducibility: The mutable OpenAI main-branch theorem source was not pinned or built in the earlier review. A reviewer-maintained ETH discussion page now contains attributed reports of pinned native executions and a cross-formalization/complexitylib port accepted by Lean’s judge and additional checkers, including a planted-wrong-statement rejection. the research desk did not rerun these artifacts. The formalized machine predicate’s equivalence to textbook ETH and the manuscript-to-formal statement correspondence remain interpretive and open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable to the source-reported theorem claim; no algorithmic benchmark comparison was inspected.

brief.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
brief.why_it_matters: If the formalized and manuscript claims are correct and match standard ETH, complexity results that rely on ETH would need reassessment. A subexponential exact algorithm would not by itself establish polynomial-time solvability or settle P versus NP.

related.summary: Anthropic’s Oct 27 preprint is a separately attributed, concurrent claim of a subexponential exact-SAT algorithm. Similarity does not establish shared evidence, identity of methods, or cross-validation.

other.title: Anthropic publishes a Claude-attributed subexponential #3-SAT algorithm claim with Lean materials
other.summary: Anthropic contributed a version-one preprint on October 27 describing a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments for fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time, including #3-SAT, and attributes the core algorithm to an internal Claude research model. Anthropic’s official repository includes the paper and a Lean 4 formalization. GitHub reports that the repository’s exact commit passed its `verify (eth)` CI workflow, which the README describes as a pinned Lean build, Comparator check and nanoda recheck. This repository-hosted result was not independently rerun here. The README explicitly says machine checks do not establish that the formal statement matches the paper; independent mathematical review remains open. The result is asymptotic and does not establish practical SAT performance. An independent external formal-methods audit later reports replaying Anthropic's exact pinned Lean proof with Lean, Comparator and nanoda, a fresh-environment replay, and a Lean bridge from the formal statement to textbook-style ETH in Anthropic's own machine model. The auditor explicitly leaves paper-to-statement and machine-model/input-encoding correspondence to prose and does not certify the paper's mathematical argument. This strengthens the reported reproducibility of the formal artifact, not the truth status of the theorem.

related.summary: The note analyzes practical constants and scope in OpenAI’s claimed ETH-refuting exact-counting result; it does not refute the asymptotic claim.

other.title: Independent note estimates extreme practical thresholds for OpenAI’s claimed ETH algorithm
other.summary: A version 1 arXiv note dated Oct 31 explains OpenAI’s claimed subexponential exact-counting result and reports that constants extracted by the authors from the Oct 25 tensor-contraction proof leave its certified running time above brute force until input sizes far beyond anything representable. The note explicitly preserves the asymptotic claim and says its separate structural limits cover the clause-product interpolation route, not the sharper parity and tensor-contraction routes. These are author-reported calculations, not independently verified results or a refutation of the headline theorem.
